Question Choices: A store has 70 pens on the shelf. In the morning, they sell 25 pens. At noon, they receive a delivery of 40 pens. In the afternoon, they sell 30 more pens. How many pens are on the shelf at the end of the day?
Hints: Morning: 70 - 25 = 45; Noon: 45 + 40 = 85; End of the day: 85 - 30 = 55
Solution: After the first sale: 70-25 = 45 pens. After the delivery: 45+40 = 85. After the last sale: 85-30 = 55 pens remain.

Question Choices: Three friends are collecting marbles. Tom has 35 marbles, Jerry has 20 more marbles than Tom, and Ann has 10 fewer marbles than Jerry. How many marbles does Ann have?
Solution: Jerry has 20 more than Tom: 35+20 = 55. Ann has 10 fewer than Jerry: 55-10 = 45 marbles.

Question Choices: A farm has 55 cows and 45 sheep. The farmer sells 30 cows and buys 20 more sheep. How many animals (cows and sheep) are on the farm now?
Solution: Update each group separately. Cows: 55-30 = 25. Sheep: 45+20 = 65. Add the new counts: 25+65 = 90 animals.

Question Choices: Alice is reading a 100-page book. On Monday she reads 20 pages. On Tuesday she reads 15 pages. On Wednesday she reads 5 pages. How many pages does she still need to read to finish the book?
Solution: Total pages read: 20+15+5 = 40. Subtract from the book total: 100-40 = 60 pages still to read.

Question Choices: A school cafeteria serves meals. Monday: 30 lunches. Tuesday: 20 more lunches than Monday. Wednesday: 10 fewer lunches than Tuesday. The cafeteria can serve 150 lunches total per week. How many lunches can they still serve Thursday and Friday combined?
Solution: Tuesday: 30+20 = 50 lunches. Wednesday: 50-10 = 40 lunches. The first three days total 30+50+40 = 120. Remaining weekly capacity: 150-120 = 30 lunches.
